prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Signing in restores any existing pets and saved progress linked to your account."]
1: ["Choose Your Pet Path", "Select whether you want to adopt a classic companion or build a custom pet."]
2: ["Your desktop companion is being prepared. It will appear on your screen as soon as setup completes."]
3: ["Meet Your New Desktop Companion"]
4: ["Right-click your pet on the desktop or system tray icon anytime to open controls, hide, or interact."]
5: ["Your Desktop Companion Awaits", "Discover how your pet lives on your desktop, reacts to your workspace, and keeps you company.", "Continue to Path Selection"]
6: ["Use a clear, brightly lit photo with a centered subject for best companion generation results."]
7: ["Sign In to Save & Sync Your Pet", "Log in to link your pet to your account and keep your progress safe across sessions."]
8: ["Tip: You can drag your pet anywhere on screen or set it to idle near your taskbar."]
9: ["Welcome to Your Desktop Companion!", "Setup is complete! Your companion is now active and ready to keep you company on your desktop."]
